reason: The cited evidence supports Inconel 718's crack resistance and bonding on H13 steel, but the hypothesis applies these findings to a different substrate (nickel-based superalloy) and much higher service temperatures without direct evidence, leaving key premises about substrate compatibility and high-temperature performance unsupported.
premises: Inconel 718 provides excellent thermal expansion matching and strong stress resistance as a transition layer on a steel substrate.
Inconel 718 transition layer prevents cracking under bending and tensile loading in laser cladding on H13 steel.
Laser-clad Inconel 718 forms a robust metallurgical bond and graded interface that alleviates stress concentration.
The cited evidence on H13 steel generalizes to nickel-based superalloy substrates under 1000–1200 °C service conditions.
